newsitem.title: INDIA: India's divestment chief cautious on asset sale.
newsitem.headline: India's divestment chief cautious on asset sale.

text.p: The chief of India's divestment commission said on Thursday that government should take note of policies under which state-owned firms operate before a partial sell-off of stakes in these units.

India plans to sell a seven percent stake in its external telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in its crude oil refining company Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) in the first round of divestment in 1996/97 (April-March).
But the government has not been able to set a date to kick-start this first round of partial sell-off of shares.

G.V. Ramakrishna, divestment commission chairman, told a news conference that these were examples of how the process should take note of policy environment in which the public sector undertakings operate.
Analysts say IOC would find it difficult to raise international funds unless the government announces a hike in petrol prices -- a move which is necessary to curb India's burgeoning oil pool deficit.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left government established the divestment commission, part of the Industry Ministry, in August to advise on the partial privatisation, or divestment, of state units.
A second round is expected to follow after the first round of sell-off of stakes in IOC and VSNL in the current fiscal year ending on March 31.
The divestment commission is not responsible for the first two rounds, but will make recommendations on divestment in 40 state-owned firms for the third tranche.
India aims to raise 50 billion rupees from divestment in 1996/97. In 1995/96, it raised only 3.57 billion rupees from the partial sell-off of shares against a target of 70 billion.

Ramakrishna said lack of in-depth study on divestment, use of proceeds to bridge fiscal deficit and sell-off of stakes to only a limited number of institutions were factors responsible for the failure of the divestment process in the past.
"Our recommendations on the 40 public sector undertakings would be ready by February end," he said.
He said the divestment commission had prepared a startegy paper on partial sell-off of stakes in state-owned firms and would hold two conferences on it.
The first conference will be held in New Delhi on January 25 and the second in Bombay on February 5.
Ramakrishna said that domestic financial institutions and foreign institutional investors would attend the conferences.
